en.title: Where English is spoken
en.summary: English around the world: where it began, where it is a first language and how it spread.

paragraphs: English began in one small country, but today it is used on every continent. About 380 million people speak it as a first language, and more than a billion use it as a second or foreign language. This lesson shows where English is spoken and why. It also practises comparisons, the passive and relative clauses.

English comes from England, where it grew from the languages of settlers from northern Europe more than 1,500 years ago. Later, ships from Britain and Ireland carried it across the sea. The countries where most people speak English as a first language are the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Ireland. In many other countries, such as India, Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa and Singapore, English is used in schools, law and government, because these countries were once part of the British Empire. English is also spoken in the Philippines, where it came with American rule.

paragraphs: **1. Comparing.** Short adjectives add -er and -est: large, larger, the largest. Long adjectives use more and most: important, more important, the most important. Use than to compare two things. English has more speakers as a second language than as a first language. See Introduction to Grammar: Adjectives and comparison.

**2. The passive in the present.** To say what people do with a language in general, use am, is or are and the past participle. English is spoken in many countries. It is used in schools. The doer, people, is not important, so it is not named. See Introduction to Grammar: Voice, reflexive and impersonal verbs.

**3. Relative clauses add information.** Use who for people, which or that for things, and where for places. In the text, the countries where most people speak English as a first language are listed. A relative clause comes straight after the noun it describes. See Introduction to Grammar: Conjunctions and linking clauses.

items: British and American English spell some words differently: **colour** and **color**, **centre** and **center**.
Some words differ too: a British **lift** is an American **elevator**, and a British **flat** is an American **apartment**.
English has taken many words from the places where it is spoken. **Bungalow**, **shampoo** and **jungle** all came from languages of India.

paragraphs: There is no single correct accent. A person from Glasgow, Dublin, Texas, Sydney or Mumbai sounds different, and all of them speak English. The best accent for a learner is one that other people can easily understand.
